items.title: [ECG] Invitation to Participate in NTU MSE's Materials Innovation Challenge 2026
items.author: Lee Meng Choo
items.description:
Message posted on behalf of NTU
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Students,
We are excited to announce Materials Innovation Challenge (MIC) 2026 – a team-based competition to turn everyday campus problems into INNOVATING solutions.
📅 Event Dates
Workshops: 2, 9, 16 September 2026 (7 PM – 9 PM)
Competition: 28 September – 1 Oct 2026 (9 AM – 6 PM)
📍 Venue: NTU campus
Why You Should Join:
🧠 Design and create prototypes to solve real-world problems
👥 Team up across levels – collaborate and meet other NTU and pre-university students
🖨️ Get hands-on guidance in 3D printing from our mentors
🤩 Meet industry experts in 3D printing
🏆 Win up to $1,500 in cash prizes
All participants will learn the necessary skills for creating the prototypes in the challenge. You will require a computer for the activities in the workshops.
Let us know if you need assistance.
🔗 Register here:
Materials Innovation Challenge 2026 – Participant Sign-Up Form  – Fill out form
🕒 Deadline: 16 August 2026
⚠️ Limited slots available – confirmation is on a first-come, first-served basis! An email with further details will be sent to you nearer the event date.
❓ For enquiries about this event, email msestudentlife@ntu.edu.sg
This is your chance to gain hands-on experience in 3D printing and foster meaningful connections in a fun-filled event. We look forward to seeing you! 😊
Warm regards,
Materials Innovation Challenge 2026 Organising Committee

items.title: Project Apricot OT Recruitment
items.author: QI WEI
items.description:
Hey Hwa Chong! 🌟
Looking for a meaningful way to serve the elderly in our community? 👵👴 Join us in continuing our Service Learning project with St. Andrew's Senior Care (SASC) at Henderson. SASC supports seniors with physical, cognitive, and social care needs, helping them age with dignity in their own communities. 🏡 Many of these seniors experience loneliness, cognitive decline, and communication barriers, and they deeply benefit from regular companionship and engaging activities. 💬❤️
As part of the Organising Team, you will foster intergenerational bonds by conducting cognitive games 🧠, gentle exercises 🤸, and adaptive activities tailored to their abilities. 🎨 You will also create opportunities to express mutual gratitude, helping to lift their emotional well-being. 😊 This project is a chance to brighten someone's day ☀️, build meaningful connections 🤝, and learn the power of patience and empathy. If you believe in making every senior feel seen and valued, step forward to lead this project and make it your own. 🌱✨
What are you waiting for? Apply for the Organising Team today! 🚀
🔗
https://forms.gle/1vC8UA92GrkxmNv47
📅 Deadline: 3/8/26 2359 ⏰
Only the team leader has to sign up. You will go through a round of interviews before you are selected. Thank you! 🙏

items.title: Inspiring Excellence 2026: Celebrating the Class of 2025
items.author: Tan Wei Ping Kenny
items.description:
Dear Hwa Chong,
Following the successful conclusion of Awards Presentation Day (APD) 2026, we invite you to celebrate the achievements of the Class of 2025 through our latest publication:
Inspiring Excellence 2026
.
This booklet captures our graduated seniors' stories, showcasing their leadership, resilience, compassion and excellence across science research, community service, the arts, sports and global competitions. To our current students: may these journeys spark your own dreams and determination, so your story might one day be featured on these pages.
APD is a special time to honour excellence, cherish guidance and inspire graduates to grow in purpose and heart, strengthening the bonds of our Hwa Chong community.
Thanks to the students of the Publications Society for producing this booklet, the seniors who shared their stories, and the APD 2026 Organising Committee for their contributions.
Warm regards,
Mr Kenny Tan
Teacher-in-Charge,
Publications Society

items.title: [Sustainability] College Recycling Competition
items.author: Kan Jia Hui Jaslyn
items.description:
The High School and College Green Councils are excited to launch this year’s College Recycling Competition!
📅 Competition Period: Term 3, Week 4 – Week 8
This competition is open to all J1 and J2 classes, where each level will compete to see who can recycle the most plastic bottles.
How to Participate 🥤
1. Finish your drink.
2. Rinse your plastic bottle with tap water.
3. Dispose of it in the CORA recycling bin located outside the Café.
Every recycled bottle contributes to your level’s total!
❓Not sure how to use the CORA bin?
Check out our quick guide on @hc_greencouncil: https://www.instagram.com/p/DaX3jbAFPm2/?igsh=bDRnMXBheTc1cmE=
At the end of the competition, all classes in the winning level will receive attractive prizes!
More importantly, this competition is an opportunity for all of us to show that small actions, when repeated by an entire cohort, can make a meaningful difference. The next time you finish a drink, take a few extra seconds to recycle your bottle instead of throwing it into the general bin.
Together, let’s build a greener Hwa Chong! 🌍💚
Presented to you by….
17th Green Council

items.title: Most Caring Teacher Award (MCTA) 2026 <Nurturing Minds, Touching Hearts>
items.author: Yee Weng Hong
items.description:
Dear students,
What is the best Teachers' Day gift you can present to your teachers this year?
A teacher may have a greater impact on your life than you can imagine. A teacher does not just impart book knowledge and nurture minds. Through the many little kind words and acts each day, a teacher cares for you and helps to raise your spirit and support your learning.
Was there a time when you felt down, and a word or act from a teacher cheered you up? Was there a time when you felt lost and aimless, and a teacher showed you the right direction to take?
Now you have the best opportunity to express your gratitude, by nominating them for the Most Caring Teacher Award 2026 ! The recipients will receive their awards on Teachers' Day 2026.
Please take some time to reflect on the roles that your teacher(s) play and submit your nomination(s) consisting of 2-3 instances when you think your teacher has displayed care and kindness. Individually, please do not submit a nomination for the same teacher more than once, as that will be a duplication of the same nomination. You may submit nominations for different teachers, if you have more than one deserving teacher in mind.
Your write up should be about 100 to 200 words. You may do so directly on ISP.
For College Section, go to ‘Most Caring Teacher Award’ link under ‘Student Services’.
For High School Section, go to ‘Awards for Teachers’ link under ‘Student Services’. Click "Add Nomination".
All write-ups will be given to the nominated teachers, and this will be an excellent Teachers' Day gift that you can give to your teachers.
Your nominations should be submitted on ISP by 7 August 2026 (Fri).
Mr Yee Weng Hong
(On behalf of the MCTA organizing committee 2026)
